rejected.title: Simultaneous equations
card: Simultaneous equations are two equations with two unknowns, such as \(x\) and \(y\). The solution is the pair of values that makes both equations true.
Substitution
Make one unknown the subject of one equation, then put it into the other. For \(y = 2x\) and \(x + y = 9\): \(x + 2x = 9\), so \(x = 3\). Then \(y = 2 \times 3 = 6\).
Elimination

Add or subtract the equations so one unknown cancels. For \(x + y = 10\) and \(x - y = 4\): adding gives \(2x = 14\), so \(x = 7\). Then \(y = 3\). If the signs of the unknown to cancel are the same, subtract.
Graphs
Each equation is a straight line. The solution is the point where the two lines cross. The lines \(y = x + 1\) and \(y = -x + 5\) cross at \((2, 3)\).

4.alt: The lines y = x + 1 and y = -x + 5 cross at the point (2, 3).

rejected.remember: The solution is one pair of values that fits both equations. It is also where the two lines cross.

a.q: Solve \(x + y = 12\) and \(x - y = 2\). What is the value of \(x\)?
a.why: Adding the equations cancels \(y\): \(2x = 14\), so \(x = 7\). The value 5 is \(y\), not \(x\).
a.clue: Add the two equations so that \(y\) cancels.

b.q: Mia buys 2 pens and 1 ruler for $7, and 1 pen and 1 ruler for $5. How much does one pen cost?
b.why: Subtract the second purchase from the first: one pen costs \$2. Then the ruler costs \$3, which is the tempting wrong option because it is the price of the other item.
b.clue: Subtract one purchase from the other so the rulers cancel.

version.title: Simultaneous equations
card: Simultaneous equations are two equations with the same two unknowns. The solution is the one pair of values that makes both equations true at once.
Substitution
make one unknown the subject of one equation and put it into the other. For \(y = 2x\) and \(x + y = 9\): \(x + 2x = 9\), so \(x = 3\) and \(y = 6\).
Elimination
add or subtract the equations so one unknown cancels. For \(x + y = 10\) and \(x - y = 4\), adding gives \(2x = 14\), so \(x = 7\) and \(y = 3\).
Graphs
each equation is a straight line, and the solution is the point where the lines cross. The lines \(y = x + 1\) and \(y = 5 - x\) cross at \((2, 3)\).
version.remember: Find the one pair of values that fits both equations: substitute, eliminate, or read where the lines cross.

a.q: Solve \(y = x + 4\) and \(2x + y = 13\). What is the value of \(y\)?
a.why: Substitute \(y = x + 4\) into the second equation: \(2x + x + 4 = 13\), so \(3x = 9\) and \(x = 3\). Then \(y = 3 + 4 = 7\). The value 3 is \(x\), not \(y\).
a.clue: Replace \(y\) in the second equation with \(x + 4\).

b.q: At a canteen, 3 pies and 2 drinks cost $16, and 1 pie and 2 drinks cost $8. How much is one pie?
b.why: Subtracting the second order from the first cancels the drinks: 2 pies cost $8, so one pie costs $4. Then each drink costs $2. Answering $8 forgets that the $8 buys two pies.
b.clue: Subtract one order from the other so the drinks cancel.
